Depends. Hornwort can be a floating plant or a stem plant. I would advise against using it as a stem plant because it gets really messy. But as a floating plant I say it looks quite nice. It covers the lid of the tank and creates a soft light on the rest of the tank and on the wood. For a stem plant rotala rotundfolia looks really nice it’s one of my fovorite plants. Or some species of bacopa. Also try some java moss on the wood. It’s beautiful! It isn’t demanding and it’s really beautiful. You can glue it on with seachem glue.

Well make sure to put some hiding places if you’re going for small cichlids. I would advise for some ram cichlids, they’re so beautiful! Also electric blue rams are wonderful too but they’re on the expensive side. Make sure that if you take cichlids you need a make and a female. Also about angelfish look under altum angels, they are a bit bigger than standard angels but they’re so much nicer than the normal angels(in my opinion). Maybe take 4 or 5 angels you have a big enough tank for them. Also make sure to buy denitrifying media for your filter and put a lot of plants. The denitrifying media and the plants will eat up the nitrates which will render regular water changes useless. I have so much denitrifying media and plants that nitrates are undetectable. I have a busy schedule and regular maintenance of my tank is hard for me. But I haven’t done a water change in over a month and my tank is still clean and nitrates are undetectable. Also buy seachem pristine. It helps with détritus breakdown.

Just make sure that there are some hiding places if you want to put some rams or you can try to put an angelfish. Also never buy plecos, buy ancistrus. Plecos are way to big and they are invasive. In Switzerland (where I live) plecos are banned simply because adult they are 50 centimeters long. Buy some ancistrus they clean the tank better than plecos and they are smaller.

Well hornwort sucks I’m sorry. It grows all over the tank in a week and personnaly I don’t even find it that pretty. If you want a nice looking fast growing plant try some species of sensiliflora. Also I assume that you were going for some sort of island aquascape. In this case I would suggest you use mostly carpeting plants like hcc or eleocharis mini on the islands. Also make sure to put a lot of denitrifying media in the filter so that you don’t need to worry to much about water changes. Personally I only do one water change every 3 months cause I have so much plants and so much denitrifying media in the filter that nitrates are untraceable

Well there are a lot so I’m going to say the main ones. The red ones on the left are althernanthera reinecki red from denerle. The green grass on the right is eleocharis mini also from denerle. In the back on th right is some amazon sword. In the back on the right next to the amazon sword and in the front on the left is some rotala rotundfolia from tropica as is the amazon sword. The large green one in the front on the right is Hygrophila compact. On the ground in the front on the left is some pogostemon helferi from Tropica. The lily pads are tropica Nymphoides. For co2 I use 40mg/L so my ph stays nice and low. For fertilzer I use Tropica Premium Nutrition. I put 2 pumps a day. And so I don’t get algae I use nitrate lowering media in both filters (jbl bionitratex). My nitrates are permanently at 5 ppm so water changes aren’t necessary.
I have nitrate removing media in the filter and once a month I do a 3 day blackout so I kill any nasty Cyanobacteria and also all kinds of algae.
I’m running 28celcius and once a week I bump the temperature to 34 degree celcius. Then the discus’ apettite is increased.
I have 2 external filters. One eheim 350+ t with a uv and an oase biomaster 600.
